name: EPYC CPU inference wastes ~92% of bandwidth if every memory channel is not populated
symptom: A Genoa/EPYC box bought for CPU LLM inference delivers a tiny fraction of its expected tok/s when the DIMM slots are not fully populated. llama.cpp discussion #3167 measured a Genoa box with ONE 64GB DIMM at 1.5 tok/s on 34B Q4_0, jumping to 4 tok/s with just a second stick.
root_cause: CPU LLM decode is memory-bandwidth-bound - the spec that matters is channels x MT/s, not cores. A 12-channel Genoa socket derives its ~460 GB/s from all 12 DDR5 channels working in parallel. One DIMM lights only one channel (~1/12 of the bandwidth), wasting ~92% of what was paid for.
workaround: Populate every channel: budget 12x 32GB or 12x 64GB for Genoa, not 4x 96GB. Use llama.cpp/ik_llama.cpp's `--numa distribute` (and RPC for dual-socket). Note dual-socket does not double 70B decode - NUMA domain splitting gives ~1.3-1.6x a single socket unless the model spans both sockets' memory evenly.
notes: Compounded by the 2026 DRAM crisis: 64GB DDR5 RDIMMs went ~$873 (Q1) toward a projected ~$1,586 (Q4), so the RAM for a proper 384GB 12-channel build is $4,000-5,200+ - more than four used RTX 3090s. This kills the CPU-inference value play unless you already own the RAM. Fully-populated Genoa measured ~7 tok/s on 70B Q4_K_M (record comm-epyc-9554-llama33-70b-q4-decode).
